children.title: Operator Range Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Operator-theoretic regimes for equality and conic constraints.

children.title: Surjectivity Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Operator qualification regimes based on onto linearizations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces.
\(G:X\to Y\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable near \(\bar x\), with \(G(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The surjectivity qualification is \(DG(\bar x)X=Y\), which yields a linear residual estimate for the derivative.

notation.meaning: Derivative of the constraint mapping at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space regularity condition for smooth equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The surjectivity qualification at \(\bar x\) is
\[
DG(\bar x)X=Y.
\]
Writing \(A=DG(\bar x)\), the Banach open-mapping theorem then gives a constant \(\kappa>0\) such that
\[
d(h,A^{-1}(y))\leq\kappa\lVert Ah-y\rVert
\]
for all \((h,y)\in X\times Y\). In particular, \(d(h,\ker A)\leq\kappa\lVert Ah\rVert\), providing the linear openness and inverse-stability required by the qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth equality system satisfies the surjectivity qualification when its derivative maps the entire decision space onto the constraint space.
knowledge_statements.title: Surjectivity Qualifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Derivative surjectivity is an appropriate Banach-space qualification, and the displayed linear estimate is valid for a bounded surjective linear operator. The condition and its open-mapping consequence have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Closed-Range Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Operator qualification regimes based on closed image structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces.
\(A:X\to Y\) is bounded and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ran}A\) is closed if and only if \(d(x,\ker A)\leq\kappa\lVert Ax\rVert\) for some \(\kappa\) and every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Quotient norm induced by the kernel.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-range criterion expressed as a quotient-space error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed-range qualification is that \(\operatorname{ran}A\) is closed in \(Y\). This holds if and only if there exists \(\kappa\geq0\) such that
\[
d(x,\ker A)\leq\kappa\lVert Ax\rVert\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Equivalently, the induced bijection \(\widetilde A:X/\ker A\to\operatorname{ran}A\), defined by \(\widetilde A[x]=Ax\), has a bounded inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded operator has closed range exactly when its output norm controls distance from each input to the operator kernel.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Range Qualifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-range criterion and quotient-space formulation are standard for bounded operators between Banach spaces, and condition is suitable for this qualification leaf. No authoritative source or inspectable locator is provided.

children.title: Equality-Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operator-theoretic qualifications for infinite-dimensional equalities.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Hilbert spaces.
\(G:X\to Y\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable, \(G(\bar x)=0\), and \(DG(\bar x)\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is locally a smooth manifold with tangent space \(\ker DG(\bar x)\) and normal space \(\operatorname{ran}DG(\bar x)^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular-value regime for smooth equalities in Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated surjectivity qualification, the implicit-function theorem makes \(M=G^{-1}(0)\) a continuously differentiable manifold near \(\bar x\). Its tangent and normal spaces satisfy
\[
T_M(\bar x)=\ker DG(\bar x),
\qquad
N_M(\bar x)=\bigl(\ker DG(\bar x)\bigr)^\perp=\operatorname{ran}DG(\bar x)^*.
\]
The last range is closed because \(DG(\bar x)\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surjective equality derivative makes the feasible set locally a smooth manifold whose tangent and normal spaces come from the derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constraint Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With Hilbert spaces and a surjective derivative, the local manifold, tangent-space, and adjoint-range normal-space claims are coherent, and property fits the regime container. These nontrivial infinite-dimensional conclusions require a cited implicit-function or regular-value result with a specific locator.

children.title: Conic-Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Range-based qualifications for infinite-dimensional cone constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces, and \(K\subset Y\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(G:X\to Y\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable near feasible \(\bar x\), with \(G(\bar x)\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robinson's conic qualification is \(0\in\operatorname{int}(G(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)X-K)\).

notation.meaning: Continuous dual cone of the constraint cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robinson qualification for a smooth mapping constrained to a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the constraint \(G(x)\in K\), Robinson's conic constraint qualification at \(\bar x\) is
\[
0\,\in\,\operatorname{int}\bigl(G(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)X-K\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, the linearized mapping \(h\mapsto G(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)h-K\) is open at \((0,0)\). When \(K=\{0\}\), this condition reduces to the surjectivity of \(DG(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robinson's conic qualification requires the linearized feasible-displacement set to contain a neighborhood of zero; equalities reduce it to derivative surjectivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Constraint Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Robinson's interior condition is appropriately formulated as a conic qualification, and its equality specialization is plausible. No source supports either the condition or the asserted equivalence with openness of the set-valued linearization, so the exact formulation cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Sequential Normal Compactness Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Compactness regimes supporting normal and coderivative calculus.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space, \(\Omega\subset X\) is locally closed, and \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
\(\widehat N_\Omega(x)\) denotes the Fréchet normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak-star vanishing Fréchet normals along \(\Omega\) must vanish in norm.

notation.meaning: Fréchet normal cone to the set at a point.
Weak-star convergence in the dual space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-based sequential normal compactness at a reference point.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.4 Sequential Normal Compactness of Sets p. 27
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Sequential Normal Compactness of Set Intersections and Inverse Images p. 341
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The set \(\Omega\) is sequentially normally compact at \(\bar x\) if, for every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) with \(x_k\in\Omega\) and every sequence \(x_k^*\in\widehat N_\Omega(x_k)\), the implication
\[
x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\longrightarrow}0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\lVert x_k^*\rVert\to0
\]
holds. This compactness qualification prevents nonvanishing normal mass from disappearing only in the weak-star topology and is automatic in finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential normal compactness requires weak-star convergence of nearby Fréchet normals to zero to imply their norm convergence to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Normal Compactness Qualifications

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.4 Sequential Normal Compactness of Sets p. 27
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Sequential Normal Compactness of Set Intersections and Inverse Images p. 341
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Equality-Constraint Multiplier Rules
children.top_down_role: Multiplier rules for smooth equality systems and manifolds.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:X\to Y\) are Fréchet differentiable at a local minimizer \(\bar x\) of \(f\) subject to \(G(x)=0\).
\(G(\bar x)=0\) and \(DG(\bar x):X\to Y\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\lambda\in Y^*\) such that \(Df(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)^*\lambda=0\).

notation.meaning: Lagrange multiplier in the dual constraint space.
Adjoint derivative of the equality mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space first-order multiplier rule under derivative surjectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a multiplier \(\lambda\in Y^*\) such that the Lagrangian stationarity equation
\[
Df(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)^*\lambda=0
\]
holds in \(X^*\). Equivalently, \(Df(\bar x)h=0\) for every feasible tangent direction \(h\in\ker DG(\bar x)\), and surjectivity ensures that the annihilator of \(\ker DG(\bar x)\) equals \(\operatorname{ran}DG(\bar x)^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular local minimizer of smooth equality constraints, the objective derivative is canceled by an adjoint derivative applied to a multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constraint Multiplier Rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Banach-space equality multiplier rule has sufficient stated differentiability, feasibility, local optimality, and derivative-surjectivity hypotheses, and theorem is the correct content kind for the multiplier-rules leaf. No authoritative source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Geometric-Constraint Multiplier Rules
children.top_down_role: Multiplier rules for feasible-set and inverse-image models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(F:X\to Y\) are continuously differentiable on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
\(D\subset Y\) is closed, \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) subject to \(F(x)\in D\), and the constraint mapping is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda\in N_D(F(\bar x)):\ \nabla f(\bar x)+F'(\bar x)^*\lambda=0\).

notation.meaning: limiting normal cone to the closed set D at y
adjoint of the derivative of F

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inverse-image rule under metric subregularity.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.2 Lipschitzian Stability of Constraint Systems p. 414
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(D\subset Y\) be closed, and define \(\Omega=\{x\in X:F(x)\in D\}\). Suppose \(f\) and \(F\) are continuously differentiable, \(\bar x\in\Omega\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) on \(\Omega\), and \(x\mapsto F(x)-D\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\). Then the inverse-image normal estimate and Fermat rule yield a geometric multiplier \(\lambda\) satisfying \[\lambda\in N_D(F(\bar x)),\qquad \nabla f(\bar x)+F'(\bar x)^*\lambda=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity converts local optimality over an inverse image into stationarity with a normal-cone multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Constraint Multiplier Rules

children.title: Operator-Constraint Multiplier Rules
children.top_down_role: Multiplier rules for Banach-space operator systems.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:X\to Y\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable, and \(K\subset Y\) is closed and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space multiplier rule under Robinson constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be Banach spaces and \(K\subset Y\) be closed and convex. Suppose \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:X\to Y\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable, \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(\{x:G(x)\in K\}\), and \[0\in\operatorname{int}\bigl(G(\bar x)+G'(\bar x)X-K\bigr).\] Then there exists \(\lambda\in Y^*\) such that \[\lambda\in N_K(G(\bar x)),\qquad f'(\bar x)+G'(\bar x)^*\lambda=0\quad\text{in }X^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robinson regularity for a Banach-space operator constraint guarantees a dual normal multiplier satisfying adjoint stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Constraint Multiplier Rules

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing locally Lipschitz \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\), where every \(g_i\) is locally Lipschitz. Let \(\bar x\) be a feasible local minimizer and \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). Assume that \(\mu_i\ge0\), \(\mu_i=0\) for \(i\notin I(\bar x)\), and \(0\in\sum_i\mu_i\partial_Cg_i(\bar x)\) imply \(\mu=0\). Then some \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies \[0\in\partial_Cf(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial_Cg_i(\bar x),\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]

children.title: Convex Programming KKT
children.top_down_role: Convex primal-dual optimality regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper convex functions, and the equality map \(Ax-b\) is affine.
There exists \(x^0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) with \(g_i(x^0)<0\) for all \(i\) and \(Ax^0=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible \(\bar x\) is optimal iff it admits multipliers satisfying convex subgradient stationarity and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex KKT equivalence under a Slater-type qualification.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex program \[\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad Ax=b.\] Assume the stated Slater-type qualification. A feasible point \(\bar x\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\nu\) such that \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial g_i(\bar x)+A^*\nu,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Thus, under qualification, the KKT system is both necessary and sufficient for primal optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a qualified convex program, feasibility and the convex KKT system are equivalent to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Programming KKT

children.title: Conic KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Cone-valued primal-dual systems.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, \(K\subset Y\) is a closed convex cone, and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(G:X\to Y\) are differentiable.
The normal cone uses \(N_K(y)=\{v:\langle v,z-y\rangle\le0\ \forall z\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conic KKT system is \(G(x)\in K\), \(\lambda\in K^\circ\), \(\langle\lambda,G(x)\rangle=0\), and \(\nabla f(x)+G'(x)^*\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic KKT system using the polar-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min\{f(x):G(x)\in K\}\), a primal-dual pair \((x,\lambda)\in X\times Y\) satisfies the conic KKT system when \[G(x)\in K,\qquad \lambda\in K^\circ,\qquad \langle\lambda,G(x)\rangle=0,\qquad \nabla f(x)+G'(x)^*\lambda=0.\] Equivalently, dual feasibility and complementarity state \(\lambda\in N_K(G(x))\). Under an appropriate conic constraint qualification these conditions are necessary at a local minimizer; for convex \(f\) and an affine conic constraint, they are sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic KKT combines cone feasibility, polar dual feasibility, orthogonality complementarity, and adjoint stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic KKT Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed finite-dimensional conic KKT system is internally consistent with the stated polar-cone convention, and condition is an appropriate content kind. However, the record also asserts necessity and sufficiency regimes without a cited locator or a precise conic qualification, so the complete statement requires a source.

children.title: Operator-Constraint KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Banach-space operator-constraint systems.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces, \(K\subset Y\) is closed and convex, and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(G:X\to Y\) are Fréchet differentiable.
The convex normal cone is \(N_K(y)=\{y^*:\langle y^*,z-y\rangle\le0\ \forall z\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator KKT system is \(G(x)\in K\), \(y^*\in N_K(G(x))\), and \(f'(x)+G'(x)^*y^*=0\) in \(X^*\).

notation.meaning: convex normal cone in the dual space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space KKT system for a closed convex operator constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\in X} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad G(x)\in K,\] a pair \((x,y^*)\in X\times Y^*\) is an operator-constraint KKT pair precisely when \[G(x)\in K,\qquad y^*\in N_K(G(x)),\qquad f'(x)+G'(x)^*y^*=0\quad\text{in }X^*.\] The normal-cone inclusion encodes dual feasibility and complementarity simultaneously. Necessity at a local minimizer requires a Banach-space constraint qualification, such as Robinson regularity; the displayed system itself is the primal-dual optimality interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator KKT pair satisfies primal feasibility, a dual normal-cone condition, and stationarity through the Banach adjoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Constraint KKT Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the operator-constraint KKT container and explicitly types the dual variables and adjoint. No source is provided for the Banach-space formulation or the accompanying Robinson-regularity necessity claim, so its conventions and scope remain unverified.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable.
\(h:\mathbb R^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Composite stationarity is represented by \(y\in\partial h(F(x))\) and \(0=\nabla f(x)+F'(x)^*y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual representation for a smooth-convex composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the composite problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\; f(x)+h(F(x)),\] the primal-dual composite KKT system at \(x\) introduces \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) and requires \[y\in\partial h(F(x)),\qquad 0=\nabla f(x)+F'(x)^*y.\] Equivalently, \(F(x)\in\partial h^*(y)\) and the same stationarity equation holds. Under a chain-rule qualification, such as continuity of \(h\) at a point of \(F(\mathbb R^n)\), local optimality implies this system; in convex-affine instances it also characterizes global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite KKT introduces a subgradient of the outer convex function whose pullback balances the smooth gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite KKT Systems

children.title: Nonsmooth–Composite Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between generalized-differentiable components plus composite model architecture.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz, \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) is continuously differentiable, and \(h:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) is convex and locally Lipschitz near \(F(\bar x)\).
\(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f+h\circ F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y\in\partial h(F(\bar x)):\ 0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)+F'(\bar x)^*y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-convex coupling for a nonsmooth plus composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(x)=f(x)+h(F(x))\), where \(f\) is locally Lipschitz, \(F\) is continuously differentiable, and convex \(h\) is locally Lipschitz near \(F(\bar x)\). If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(\Phi\), then Fermat's rule, the Clarke sum rule, and the composite chain rule imply that there exists \(y\in\partial h(F(\bar x))\) such that \[0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)+F'(\bar x)^*y.\] Thus nonsmooth stationarity in the primal variable is coupled to an outer-function subgradient through the adjoint derivative of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsmooth term and a convex composite term couple through an outer subgradient pulled back by the inner derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth–Composite Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coupling formula is mathematically plausible under the stated local Lipschitz and smoothness assumptions and fits the terminal container, but no source is supplied for the exact Clarke sum-and-chain-rule inference. Because that calculus step determines the asserted existence of a single outer subgradient, an authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), define the active set \[I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(x)=0\}.\] If \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and complementary slackness \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\) holds for every \(i\), then every inactive constraint has zero multiplier: \[g_i(x)<0\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda_i=0.\] Consequently, any KKT stationarity expression may be reduced to multipliers indexed by \(I(x)\); only active constraints can carry nonzero multiplier weight, although an active constraint may still have zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity restricts nonzero inequality multipliers to the active set, while active constraints may still have zero multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint Structure

children.title: Complementary-Slackness Structure
children.top_down_role: Organization of multiplier–slack relationships within KKT representations.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), primal feasibility gives \(g_i(x)\le0\) and dual feasibility gives \(\lambda_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complementary slackness is \(\lambda_i g_i(x)=0\), equivalently \(\lambda_i>0\Rightarrow g_i(x)=0\) and \(g_i(x)<0\Rightarrow\lambda_i=0\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative multiplier of the ith inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar complementary slackness for inequality constraints.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(g_i(x)\le0\) with multiplier \(\lambda_i\ge0\), complementary slackness is the condition \[\lambda_i g_i(x)=0.\] Writing the primal slack as \(s_i=-g_i(x)\ge0\), the same condition is \(\lambda_i s_i=0\). Hence \[\lambda_i>0\ \Longrightarrow\ g_i(x)=0,\qquad g_i(x)<0\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda_i=0.\] Applied componentwise, this condition couples primal activity to dual support without requiring every active constraint to possess a positive multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary slackness says a constraint's nonnegative slack and nonnegative multiplier cannot both be positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Slackness Structure

children.title: Saddle-Point Representation
children.top_down_role: KKT systems interpreted through Lagrangian saddle geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are convex on \(C\).
A constraint qualification ensuring strong Lagrange duality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L(\bar x,\lambda)\le L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\le L(x,\bar\lambda)\qquad\forall x\in C,\ \forall\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex differentiable program with inequality constraints and strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible primal-dual pair \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfies the KKT conditions if and only if it is a saddle point of the Lagrangian: \(L(\bar x,\lambda)\le L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\le L(x,\bar\lambda)\) for all \(x\in C\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). In that case, \(f(\bar x)=\inf_{x\in C}L(x,\bar\lambda)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in C}L(x,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under convexity and strong duality, KKT pairs are exactly Lagrangian saddle points, and their saddle value equals the primal and dual optimal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closure criterion for multiplier sets represented by continuous stationarity equations and closed sign constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(\{0\}\) and \(K\) are closed and \(R\) is continuous, the set \(\Lambda=R^{-1}(\{0\})\cap K\) is closed. In the finite-dimensional multiplier space \(Y=\mathbb{R}^q\), the Heine–Borel property therefore gives
\[
\Lambda\text{ is compact}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Lambda\text{ is bounded}.
\]
Thus boundedness alone yields compactness only after closedness of the stationarity, sign, and complementarity conditions has been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional multiplier set defined by continuous equations and closed sign constraints is closed, so compactness is exactly boundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Requirements for Compactness

children.title: Multiplier-Mapping Stability
children.top_down_role: Continuity, calmness, and Lipschitzian behavior of multiplier mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Mapping Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local stability notions for a parameterized set-valued multiplier mapping between normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be a neighborhood of \(\bar p\) in \(P\), let \(V\) be a neighborhood of \(\bar y\) in \(Y\), and let \(\mathbb{B}_Y\) be the closed unit ball of \(Y\). The mapping \(\Lambda\) is calm at \((\bar p,\bar y)\) if there exist such \(U,V\) and \(L\geq 0\) satisfying
\[
\Lambda(p)\cap V\subset \Lambda(\bar p)+L\lVert p-\bar p\rVert\mathbb{B}_Y\qquad(p\in U).
\]
It has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar y)\) if there exist such \(U,V\) and \(L\geq 0\) satisfying
\[
\Lambda(p_1)\cap V\subset \Lambda(p_2)+L\lVert p_1-p_2\rVert\mathbb{B}_Y\qquad(p_1,p_2\in U).
\]
It is outer semicontinuous at \(\bar p\) if, whenever \(p_k\to\bar p\), \(y_k\to y\), and \(y_k\in\Lambda(p_k)\), one has \(y\in\Lambda(\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calmness gives a one-sided local Lipschitz estimate from the reference parameter, the Aubin property gives a two-parameter local Lipschitz estimate, and outer semicontinuity preserves membership under convergent graph sequences.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Y\) are normed spaces.
\(\Lambda:P\rightrightarrows Y\) is a set-valued mapping and \(\bar y\in\Lambda(\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditions define calmness at \((\bar p,\bar y)\), the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar y)\), and outer semicontinuity at \(\bar p\), respectively.

notation.meaning: Closed unit ball in the multiplier space
Reference graph point of the multiplier mapping
Neighborhoods of the reference parameter and multiplier, respectively

assumptions_latex: The smooth constraints are \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\).
The point \(\bar x\) is feasible, with active set \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional MFCQ failure characterized by a nonzero abnormal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification fails at \(\bar x\) precisely when there exists \((\lambda,\mu)\neq(0,0)\) such that
\[
\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\nabla h_j(\bar x)=0,
\qquad \lambda_i\geq0\quad(i\in I(\bar x)).
\]
Equivalently, either the equality gradients are linearly dependent or no direction \(d\) satisfies \(\nabla h_j(\bar x)^Td=0\) for every \(j\) and \(\nabla g_i(\bar x)^Td<0\) for every \(i\in I(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ fails exactly when a nonzero abnormal multiplier balances the active constraint gradients without an objective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The smooth finite-dimensional theorem-of-alternatives characterization of MFCQ failure is correctly scoped and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the nontrivial equivalence has no inspectable source.

Suppose
\[
\sum_i d_{\lambda,i}\nabla g_i(\bar x)+\sum_j d_{\mu,j}\nabla h_j(\bar x)=0,

where \(d_{\lambda,i}\geq0\) for active inequalities, \(d_{\lambda,i}=0\) for inactive inequalities, and \((d_\lambda,d_\mu)\neq(0,0)\). Then every normal multiplier \((\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\) generates the ray

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex characterization of unbounded multiplier sets by recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the recession cone by
\[
C^\infty:=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^q:z+td\in C\ \text{for every}\ z\in C\ \text{and}\ t\geq0\}.
\]
Then
\[
C\text{ is unbounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C^\infty\neq\{0\}.
\]
Consequently, unboundedness of a closed convex multiplier set is witnessed by a single nonzero direction along which every multiplier can be extended indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex multiplier set is unbounded exactly when its recession cone contains a nonzero direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar rank-loss example showing multiplier blow-up and failure of local boundedness, while distinguishing these phenomena from outer semicontinuity and calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\Lambda(t):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}:1+t\lambda=0\}.
\]
Then \(\Lambda(t)=\{-1/t\}\) for \(t\neq0\), whereas \(\Lambda(0)=\varnothing\). Hence every sequence \(t_k\to0\) with \(t_k\neq0\) has associated multipliers satisfying \(\lvert\lambda_k\rvert=1/\lvert t_k\rvert\to\infty\), so \(\Lambda\) is not locally bounded at \(0\). This example does not violate sequential outer semicontinuity at \(0\), and calmness at \(0\) cannot be asserted or denied without a reference multiplier in \(\Lambda(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solutions of 1+tλ=0 blow up as t approaches zero, proving failure of local boundedness. The example does not establish failure of outer semicontinuity, and calmness has no reference graph point at zero.
assumptions_latex: For \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), define the scalar multiplier mapping by \(\Lambda(t)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}:1+t\lambda=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mapping \(\Lambda\) is not locally bounded at \(0\); the example does not refute outer semicontinuity there, and calmness at \((0,\bar\lambda)\) is inapplicable because \(\Lambda(0)=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct scalar calculation establishes blow-up and failure of local boundedness

knowledge_statements.title: Equilibrium-Constraint Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of standard NLP MFCQ for the smooth product reformulation of complementarity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a complementarity pair represented by
\[
-G_i(x)\leq0,\qquad -H_i(x)\leq0,
\qquad G_i(x)H_i(x)=0,
\]
the standard smooth nonlinear-programming reformulation fails the Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification at every complementarity-feasible point \(\bar x\). This includes points with \(G_i(\bar x)=0<H_i(\bar x)\), points with \(H_i(\bar x)=0<G_i(\bar x)\), and biactive points with \(G_i(\bar x)=H_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating complementarity as two ordinary inequalities and a smooth product equality causes the standard nonlinear-programming reformulation to fail MFCQ at every complementarity-feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(G_i\) and \(H_i\) are continuously differentiable near a complementarity-feasible point \(\bar x\).
The complementarity pair is represented by \(-G_i(x)\leq0\), \(-H_i(x)\leq0\), and \(G_i(x)H_i(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard smooth nonlinear-programming reformulation fails MFCQ at every complementarity-feasible point \(\bar x\).
